utterances.text: I suppose an easier way to introduce a topic that relates to an agreed fact is to put the agreed fact to the witness and tell him that that's an agreed fact and he can comment whichever way he wants to comment, rather than ask him, when he says he doesn't know, then you tell him later again that you're telling him that it is so. In one swoop you can just say: This happened on such and such a date, that's an agreed fact, what's your comment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not know what the witness knew, what he did not know. This statement does not refer to this date, so I'm not going to go on. I will just move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the summer of 1991, in the beginning of the autumn of 1991, throughout Croatia there were blockades of and then attacks at JNA barracks. Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: That could be seen on television too. It is a well-known thing that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What television and what was it that you saw, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: We were watching Croatian television then, our television, Croatian television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What was it that you saw on television? What was this about? What kind of blockades or barracks and whose barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, blockades of the JNA army, the barracks of the JNA army. That was the only army then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Was this a blockade of JNA barracks that were deployed in the Republic of Croatia until then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, you know, I would like you to ask me about the area that I know about -- I mean Plasko. If you mean these barracks that I'm talking about in Plasko, in Licka Jesenica. I already made my statement how this went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I will have to caution you that it is the Defence that decides what questions it's going to put to you, not the questions that you like or dislike. You are duty-bound to answer the questions put by the Defence, just like those put by the Prosecution. Did you hear that in --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I don't think the witness said he didn't want what questions he disliked; I understood what he said that he would like questions about things he knows about. I don't think it's fair for counsel to suggest that he likes questions and he doesn't want certain questions because he dislikes them. I think that's misstating what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think that's -- I think that's a fair reflection of what the witness said, Mr. Milovancevic. And while I'm on the floor, may I just, once again, remind you that you are still -- although you said you were making preparations to go into the Martic police issue, you've still not got into it. You're still sort of cross-examining all over the show. May you please get to that point which you're allowed to cross-examine on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend the Prosecutor asked the witness during his examination-in-chief about the attack on the barracks in Licka Jesenica. This is a barracks and a fuel depot of the JNA. I'm trying to talk about that subject, too, but the Defence does not believe that that is an isolated incident. Through the witness it is trying to get to the following information, whether this was part of attacks throughout Croatia and whether the witness knew about that. And then we will move on to Licka Jesenica. Was that the reason why an attack was launched against Saborsko. So I will try to be as accurate as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were mobilised into the Territorial Defence in Plasko in August or September. You say you were mobilised, and you said that this was self-organisation. Was there a Territorial Defence unit in Plasko until that moment, until the moment when you were mobilised in accordance with previous plans of the Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes, but all of that was within the municipality of Ogulin, the level of the municipality of Ogulin. We then belonged to the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Ogulin, but in Plasko, no, because we didn't have a municipality, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: How far away is Ogulin from Plasko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: 28 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a Territorial Defence in Ogulin as there was in Yugoslavia before, or was there the ZNG and the police of the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Until this began, this unbearable situation began, it was like it was anywhere else in Yugoslavia. The Territorial Defence was organised in the municipality of Ogulin as it was elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand what you said correctly. If I say -- if I interpret this in the following way: That you said just now that until this crisis broke out in the 1990s in the municipality of Ogulin there was a normal Territorial Defence just like in all the other municipalities in Yugoslavia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in the municipality of Ogulin there was an organisation of the ZNG, the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I could not say anything with certainty about that. A lot of things were being said, but how much truth was involved is very hard to say now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Milovancevic please slow down and pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Was it only said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are being asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Were people talking about -- well, we are now talking about what people were talking about. What were people saying, that the ZNG did exist and that they were there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, you know all of that very well. At the Maksimir stadium there was a promotion of the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At that time in Ogulin, in August/September 1991, were there any Croat police forces there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, yes. I explained earlier on that precisely in 1990 or the end of 1990 or beginning of 1991 a group of police came back and was formed in Plasko, but the MUP was in Ogulin. But it was just this one department that was open in Plasko before all of these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This police of the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia in Ogulin, what was their name and what kind of insignia did they have on their sleeves in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Like now, "MUP of Croatia, MUP Hrvatski."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is part of their insignia the Croatian chequer-board flag, the chequer-board emblem, traditional chequer-board emblem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At that time what about the policemen of Serb ethnicity who worked in the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia? Were they laid off, dismissed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: As for Plasko, what I can say with certainty, allegedly they were trying to have proportionate representation of the Croatian population and the Serb population, and that was at the Plaski police station, too, among the policemen. Now, I don't know exactly but there were about nine Serbs and three Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was it that the police station of Plaski or police outpost of Plaski was established where there were no more Croatian policemen, policemen of Croat ethnicity, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I already said that I do not know exactly when the police was established exactly, but it certainly operated with a mixed composition all the way up to what happened in Plitvice. And after these events the ethnic Croat policemen could no longer come, and they didn't come to work, to work at the police station in Plaski.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that after the events in Plitvice on the 1st of April, 1991, in Plasko there were no more Croatian policemen. And do you know whether in Saborsko a police outpost was being established of the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how big that police outpost in -- was, how many policemen were employed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that at one point in time the barracks in Licka Jesenica were attacked, and you also said when answering the Prosecutor's questions that this was during the summer, if I understood you correctly, of 1991 and that the attack was repelled. You did not tell us who it was that launched this attack and where the attack came from and what kind of equipment was used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: It was said then that these were forces of the Croatian MUP, that's what people were saying, but I don't know. So the Croatian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear what kind of equipment were -- was used to launch the attack and from where, from what direction it was launched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: It was mortar fire before that, but the location of this barracks itself -- or, rather, the depot, it is right in the middle of the forest and there are high fir trees there. So it's from all directions -- I mean, nobody ever controlled this area in absolute terms. You cannot say: Right, this is it. This is where you can get through. So it could have been anybody, and it could have come from all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question; if you can, answer it. Was the attack launched by Serb forces or Croat forces or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe there were Serbs among them, too, who were mobilised in the Croatian -- well, I don't know. I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does this answer of yours mean that these were Croatian units or Serb units? That's what I meant "units."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Well, if I said that it was the MUP of Croatia, then I guess it can be understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it would be a good moment to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Court adjourned. Come back at 20 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I remind you once again that you have still not started cross-examining on the Martic police, and we are -- we are concerned because time is running out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we have just discussed the attack on the barracks in Licka Jesenica mounted by the Croatian police. Do you know when that happened? Could you give us a time-frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I think it was just before the attack on Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you were responding to questions from the Prosecution, mention was made of an event at Kriz. It had to do with the letter addressed to Spehar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Rudolf Spehar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Do you know who was killed at this place, Kriz --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear which Kriz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At Glibodol Kriz, was it Serbs, Bogdan Petrovic, Milan Susnjar, and Bogdan Susnjar [as interpreted] who got killed? Are those the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes. There's an error. It's not Bogdan Susnjar, it's Milan and Stevan Susnjar and Bogdan Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said they were from Plasko. Were they ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said on that day they took the forest road to buy horses. Were they wearing uniforms or civilian clothes; do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I think only Bogdan Petrovic was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that they were ambushed and butchered, killed, in an atrocious manner and many injuries were found on the mutilated bodies of these men. For instance, Bogdan's ears were cut off. He had several stabbing wounds to the stomach. And the doctor later -- the coroner later established that he took five or six hours to die. Milan had his one arm cut off and a finger of another hand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I didn't see the bodies but those were the rumours that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that they were buried in a pit and the bodies, the corpses of two horses who were also killed were thrown over their bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes, I know. People in Plasko were saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were over 150 bullet holes on the tractor and ten bullet holes on the small Fiat 750 car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement to the OTP that sometime in October or November active-duty JNA officers came and established the TO in Plasko as a separate brigade called the Plasko brigade. Was it a JNA brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: That Territorial Defence that was organised by the then-municipality of Plaski was very briefly under the command of that Nikola Dokmanovic. Very soon afterwards - but please don't take my word for it - a group of about 18 JNA officers arrived headed by this man, Trbojevic, and they set up a brigade and they called it 124th Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You did your military service and you were a member of the Territorial Defence. Do you know if the JNA and the Ministry of Defence had the sole power and authority to create such units according to the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of this operation near Saborsko on the 12th of November, 1991, you explained that just before that operation the commander of this newly established Plaski Brigade was visited by the commander of the Tactical Group 2, Cedomir Bulat, and that you found out from that visit that there would be an attack mounted on Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: I'll try to explain. In the immediate vicinity of Plasko, there was a big military training ground on the road from Plaski to Slunj. It's a large area formerly called Tobolic Zbijeg [phoen] and most of JNA troops were stationed there. In peacetime, while Yugoslavia still existed, it used to be a training ground and shooting range, and all this installation remained standing. And whenever troops of the JNA came to our area they would be stationed there. One of the officers on that training ground was Cedomir Bulat, and he often came to see Trbojevic. On the occasion of one of these visits, the rumour was started that there would be an attack on Saborsko. But I cannot tell you anything more precisely because I wasn't there. I wasn't privy to their talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So can I conclude that you were aware that Cedomir Bulat as a JNA officer came to see Petar Trbojevic, who was commander of this Plaski Brigade just before this operation, the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were describing the creation of this Plaski Brigade, you explained that until November 1991 the infantry of the Territorial Defence that would later become the Plaski Brigade had semi-automatic rifles and machine-guns in their arsenal and that every battalion had two or three mortars. Is that what you said, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You also explained that once this Plaski Brigade was established the JNA brought tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and cannons, and you explained the Plaski Brigade had six to eight tanks, five to six APCs, three Howitzers, 130-millimetres, three mortars, and ten anti-aircraft guns. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MM-037
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we need that -- a redaction of that last answer. It was very specific. Also -- also, it seems to me that the questions continue to be beyond what cross-examination is supposed to be about. These questions pertain neither to Martic's police nor, as far as I can tell, to any of the questions that I put to the witness, which I concede are fair game for cross-examination. Of course he can ask -- cross-examine on the questions that I put to the witness, but these questions that we're having now are still not about Martic's police and not about the questions that I put to the witness. And I'm just concerned about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. May that question at page 64, starting at line 6 to 8, please be redacted. Mr. Milovancevic, I think I've asked you several times to please get to the questions that you're allowed to ask the witness about. I'm now telling you, if you ask one more question that has nothing to do with what you're supposed to ask, I'm going to rule you out of order. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I take your point, but just to avoid misunderstanding, lest I be misunderstood, I'm now putting questions that have to do with the very attack on Saborsko, with that operation. It's the JNA and members of the police who took part in that operation, and I'm only trying, through the answers of the witness to these questions, to establish which unit attacked Saborsko on that day so as to get to the answer who was in command, who was subordinated, if there was any concerted action and cooperation, et (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you're once again causing a redaction. Can that statement please be redacted, that sentence starting from line 11 to line 13 of page 65. And, Mr. Milovancevic, can you please get to where you say you are getting and ask the questions that are relevant. If the Bench thinks you're asking questions that are not relevant, the Bench will rule you out of order. I don't think the Bench still wants to hear your explanations as to where you're going; just get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I ask that we move to private session now because of the nature of -- the identifying nature of my following questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of March, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
